items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: I was with a lot of maneuvering with John Hammond.

ctx.x: How did you see John Hammond? How did you feel about him when he came in there, having enough nerve to come into a black community and interested in jazz, which was basically a black art?

My first expression to him was, 'You?'. He said, 'I'm John Hammond.' I said, 'I'm Jo Jones and this is Dick Wilson. What are you coming here to see me for. You want to see Count Basie; you don't want to see me.' And he came to me; he did not go to Basie to talk anything. I said, 'Now you don't impress me as being a Great White Father.' At that particular time I did not know that he knew something about my background. This was in 1936, but John knew about my background in 1930.
What did he do for you?
